name: Getting Your Whole-House Renovation Approved: A Timeline
description: Getting Your Whole-House Renovation Approved: A Timeline

step.name: Step 1
step.text: Embarking on a whole-house interior renovation in the Denver area is exciting, but it involves several key phases, especially when permits and inspections are concerned. Here's a general timeline of what to expect to get your project approved.

step.name: Step 2
step.text: **Phase 1: Define Scope and Initial Planning.** This is where you figure out exactly what you want to change, room by room. During this phase, you'll also identify if your renovation will alter load-bearing elements, wiring, plumbing, or HVAC, as these changes will trigger specific permits. This initial planning helps determine the necessary drawings and documentation.

step.name: Step 3
step.text: **Phase 2: Documentation Preparation and Permit Submission.** Once your scope is clear, you'll prepare all required documentation, including detailed plans, product approvals, and any engineering calculations. This complete package is then submitted to your local authority having jurisdiction (AHJ). Remember, permit rules and required documents can vary by project type and location, so thoroughness here prevents delays.

step.name: Step 4
step.text: **Phase 3: Work in Inspection-Ready Phases.** After your permits are issued, construction begins! It's crucial to complete the work in phases that align with inspection requirements. For example, electrical, plumbing, and framing work are typically completed and inspected before walls are closed up. Never conceal work that hasn't been signed off on by an inspector.

step.name: Step 5
step.text: **Phase 4: Schedule and Conduct Inspections.** As each phase of work is completed, you (or your contractor) will schedule the required inspections. Many jurisdictions require inspections to be scheduled in advance, often with a day's notice. Be prepared for the inspector by having approved plans on-site and ensuring all areas are accessible. Some jurisdictions also have time limits on permit validity, so keep your project moving.

step.name: Step 6
step.text: **Phase 5: Final Inspections and Closeout.** Once all major construction is complete, final inspections for each trade will occur. This is where the AHJ confirms that all work meets code and is completed according to the approved plans. Successful final inspections lead to project closeout and final approval. Coordinating all these steps effectively is where a professional general contractor really shines.
